item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a 2024 source showing Abiy’s term limits or succession rules being directly tested. I also did not find evidence of an actual constitutional handover of power in 2024; the year mostly shows continuity under Abiy, with procedural elections at the margins and strong emergency-rule behavior elsewhere.","evidence":[{"title":"Ethiopia: Freedom in the World 2025 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2025","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-world/2025","summary":"Freedom House says the prime minister is selected by the largest party after parliamentary elections, and notes that some outstanding legislative and regional elections held in June 2024 were peaceful and credible according to AU observers. This is the strongest positive evidence for procedural continuity, not for an actual transfer of power.","question_ids":["4B.8","4B.2"]},{"title":"Final Observation Report on the June 24, 2024 reruns","publisher":"CECOE","date":"2024","url":"https://cecoe.org/download/final-observation-report-on-the-outstanding-and-reelections-of-the-sixth-general-elections-held-in-benishangul-gumuz-afar-somali-and-central-ethiopia-regions-in-june-24-2024/","summary":"Domestic observers described the June 24 rerun elections as transparent enough for systematic observation, with broad observer deployment and monitoring of polling, counting, and the post-election environment. This is positive but narrow evidence of constitutional process under constrained conditions.","question_ids":["4B.8","4B.2"]},{"title":"The state-of-emergency proclamation centralized coercive authority","publisher":"ENA English","date":"2024-11-03","url":"https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124","summary":"The proclamation centralized authority under an operation command, allowed replacement of local administrators, restricted CSOs and media suspected of aiding “terrorist” groups, and suspended normal judicial handling of enforcement. That is evidence of consolidation through emergency rule, not respectful constitutional transfer.","question_ids":["4B.8","4B.5","4B.6","4B.4"]},{"title":"Reuters reported a secret security committee interfering in the justice system","publisher":"Reuters via EHRC","date":"2024-02-27","url":"https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/","summary":"Reuters, via the EHRC, reported a secret “Koree Nageenyaa” committee that interfered in the justice system and was linked to widespread human-rights violations. This is strong evidence of extra-constitutional coercive power, which cuts against orderly succession and lawful transfer.","question_ids":["4B.8","4B.4","4B.5"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Ethiopia","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-01-12","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia","summary":"HRW said authorities restricted social media, arrested opposition figures and journalists, and used emergency powers in ways that narrowed political space. It also noted that fighting and repression left opposition groups with little meaningful room to participate. This is negative evidence against respect for constitutional competition and succession norms.","question_ids":["4B.8","4B.2","4B.5","4B.6","4B.7"]},{"title":"Authorities suspended three rights groups while Abiy praised reforms","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-12-02","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups","summary":"HRW said the government suspended three rights groups even as Abiy publicly praised reforms like media freedom and NGO registration. That pattern points to selective coercion rather than a restrained commitment to constitutional or coalition-based rules.","question_ids":["4B.8","4B.4","4B.5","4B.6","4B.7"]}]}
